page.layout: One page of text, one column, full width. Running head at the top above the text, printed page number 196 at the left of it. Catchword at the lower right below the last line. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: ne fumendus: stomachus oleo absynthite, cui addita sit nardi spica, aut celtica robo-randus. Quod si diuturnus iam sit factus morb. & per essentiam arq; proprietatem, tunc cauftica duo fiant: unum, quod sit infra uentriculum, ut in crure: alterum in scapula, prius uapores auertet: posterius è cerebro humores deriuabit. Si ob menfium aut fecundæ retentionem, obortta sit epilepsia, curabitur medicamentis aperientibus, ut pulegii, calaminthæ, origani, sabinæ rutæ, arthemisiæ, radicis Aristolochiæ longę, aut rotundæ, decoctis, fotibus & iniectionibus, Trochiscis è myrrha, pesis ex hiera mellita, cui myrrhæ nonnihil additum sit.

Secundam quoq; deturbant sternutamenta naribus subdita, tefte Hippocrate, Aphorismo quadragesimo nono, Sectionis quintæ. Ad lecudas[?] deturbandas sternutario immisso nares, & os manu obturat. Poterit quoq; purgari corpus pilulis, quæ uterum expurgant, ut fœtidis & de agarico. A' purgatione non parum conferunt theriaca, mithridatium, & triphera magna sine opio. Nam his remediis omnibus profligari poterit comitialis morbus à feminis corruptione natus. Qui uero prægnanti contin-gic[?]

page.notes: Catchword "gic" is partly cut at the edge of the scan and is a fragment of the next word. The first word of the second paragraph, "lecudas", is probably "fecundas" in the printer's type but is marked as doubtful. Printed spellings such as "pulegij", "remedijs" and "uero" were normalised for i/j and u/v; "longę", "quoq;" and "A'" are kept as printed. The paragraph break before "Secundam" follows the short line ending "additum sit." The text runs on into the catchword line.
